title: Invertible multiplication on a smooth commutative group space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $G$ be a smooth commutative group algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Thus $G$ is an algebraic space with multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities; smoothness means smoothness on etale scheme charts. Let $n\geq1$ be an integer invertible in every local ring of $S$. The multiplication morphism $[n]:G\to G$, the sum of $n$ copies of the identity under the group law, is etale. Its kernel $G[n]=G\times_{G,[n],e}S$ is an etale group algebraic space over $S$. Formation of this kernel commutes with arbitrary base change. No properness of $G$ or finiteness of $G[n]\to S$ is asserted.

proof.text: Smoothness of $G/S$ on scheme charts includes local finite presentation. The chart criterion transfers this to $G\to S$; it is also locally of finite type, since a finitely presented algebra has finitely many generators. Apply relative local finite presentation to $X=Y=G$, $Z=S$, $f=[n]$ to see that $[n]$ is locally of finite presentation.

Fix an affine first order test $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ over $S$, with square-zero ideal $I$. The kernel $K=\ker(G(T)\to G(T_0))$ is an $A/I$-module whose addition is its group law, and $[n]|_K$ is multiplication by $n$. The section $n\in\mathcal O_S$ is a unit because it is a unit in every stalk; its local inverses are unique and glue. Its pullback to $T_0$ therefore has an inverse. Multiplication by $n$ on $K$ is bijective, with inverse multiplication by this inverse scalar.

Given $x_0\in G(T_0)$ and $y\in G(T)$ with $[n]x_0=y|_{T_0}$, smooth affine lifting supplies $x\in G(T)$ lifting $x_0$. In additive notation put $d=y-[n]x\in K$. Step 2 gives a unique $k\in K$ with $[n]k=d$. Then $x+k$ lifts $x_0$ and maps to $y$, since $G$ is commutative. If $z$ is a second such lift, $z-(x+k)\in K$ and its $n$-multiple is zero, so it is zero by step 2. This proves unique lifting for $[n]$.

source.place: Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), affine lifting; correction by the square-zero kernel of step 2.

proof.text: The map $[n]$ is locally of finite presentation by step 1 and satisfies the unique first order lifting condition by step 3. The infinitesimal criterion therefore makes $[n]:G\to G$ etale.

By step 4 and the single-diagram test for etaleness, choose surjective representable etale atlases $a:U\to G$, $b:V\to G$ from schemes and $h:U\to V$ with $bh=[n]a$; then $h$ is an etale scheme morphism. Every scheme base change of $h$ is etale, so $h$ is representable etale. Thus $h$ and $b$ are chartwise etale, hence so is $bh=[n]a$; as $U$ is a scheme, $[n]a$ is representable etale, and atlas detection (3) makes $[n]$ chartwise etale. The sheaf fibre product $G[n]=G\times_{G,[n],e}S$ is an algebraic space, and $G[n]\to S$ is chartwise etale as the base change of $[n]$ along $e$. For a surjective representable etale $a\prime:U\prime\to G[n]$ from a scheme, $U\prime\to S$ is therefore representable etale, i.e. an etale scheme morphism; with $\operatorname{id}_S$ as target chart this one diagram shows that $G[n]\to S$ is etale on charts. For every $S$-scheme $T$, its points are exactly $\{x\in G(T):[n]x=0\}$; this subset is closed under addition, inverse and zero. These operations are natural in $T$, hence define the commutative group-space structure. For $S\prime\to S$, both $G[n]\times_SS\prime$ and $G_{S\prime}[n]$ represent the same functor $T\mapsto\{x\in G(T):[n]x=0\}$ on $S\prime$-schemes, compatibly with their projections and group laws. The fibre-product universal property gives their canonical isomorphism.
